_comment: Curated Creator -> [Provider] DISTRIBUTION relation: the hosting surfaces a lab operates or brands for its OWN models. It is the Creator axis's answer to Family.CanonicalProvider, and it is deliberately NOT the set of every provider that rehosts a lab's weights -- a rehost is exactly what this relation exists to rank BELOW a first-party surface. Creator -> [Provider] is many-to-many in general, so unlike Family -> Creator it is a relation, not a function: one lab may operate several surfaces (regional splits, coding plans) and one provider slug may appear under more than one creator when a lab genuinely brands another lab's channel (google-vertex-anthropic is Anthropic's Vertex channel, so it sits under 'anthropic', not under 'google'). A multi-lab HUB is never a distribution surface here, however closely a lab is associated with it: modelscope and huggingface host many labs' weights on the same footing, so listing one under its associated lab would rank a hub above a genuine rehost for that lab's whole family set while saying nothing about first-party hosting. A creator with NO first-party surface in this catalog simply has no row here and Creator.Providers() returns an empty slice -- that is the honest answer for a weights-only lab such as BlackForestLabs or NousResearch, never an invented one. PROVIDER ORDER WITHIN A ROW IS LOAD-BEARING: it is the lab's own primacy order (primary API first, then regional splits, then plan-scoped surfaces), and resolution picks the EARLIEST listed surface present among a model's hosts. Re-sorting a row alphabetically is a behaviour change, not a formatting one. Loud-at-codegen via ValidateCreatorProviderTable (every creator must satisfy Creator.IsKnown and every provider Provider.IsKnown), graceful-at-runtime via loadCreatorProviderTableSafe. Codegen also emits parse/data/creator_providers_unserved.json listing the curated pairs that serve no instance of any of that creator's families, so a stale or aspirational row is visible rather than silent.
